$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GCP Cloud Run (services, jobs, worker pools, domain mappings). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py — a claim the backend does not honour fails CI.

gcp.run.services.scaling_billing.title: Service scaling, ingress and CPU allocation (request-based / instance-based billing)
limitations: Billing is not metered; the console mirrors the cpuIdle setting but Vyomi does not charge for instance time.

gcp.run.services.source.title: Source (inline function entry point, runtime, code)
limitations: "Save and redeploy" is enforced, not just stored: a source/runtime/entry-point edit changes the revision's image fingerprint, so the same revision-diff logic the Admin API uses for any template change cuts a real new revision (visible on the Revisions tab, traffic following it) exactly as a redeploy would.

For Python sources, Vyomi parses the code on create/update and rejects it the way a real build would fail: a syntax error or an entry point the source doesn't define returns a 400 instead of saving. Other runtimes are stored and returned as configured but not parsed.
Vyomi does not build a container image or run the code; there is no invocation (see Observability for the metrics/logs gap).

gcp.run.services.yaml.title: YAML view of the service config
limitations: The YAML view is generated read-only from the real service state; editing and re-applying YAML directly is not simulated — use the other tabs.

gcp.run.services.continuous_deployment.title: Continuously deploy from a repository (Cloud Build / GitHub) or set up continuous deployment on an existing service
limitations: Vyomi has no Cloud Build or source-repository integration.

gcp.run.services.triggers.title: Event triggers (Eventarc) and Cloud Build source deploys
limitations: Vyomi has no Eventarc or Cloud Build backend; only HTTP-style services are modelled.

gcp.run.services.observability.title: Observability (request metrics, container instance count, logs)
limitations: Vyomi does not meter real request traffic against deployed services, so there is no metrics or log data to show.

gcp.run.jobs.yaml.title: YAML view of the job config
limitations: The YAML view is generated read-only from the real job state; editing and re-applying YAML directly is not simulated.

gcp.run.jobs.observability.title: Job observability (execution metrics, logs)
limitations: Vyomi does not meter real container execution, so there is no metrics or log data to show.

gcp.run.jobs.triggers.title: Job triggers (Eventarc, Cloud Scheduler bindings shown on the job)
limitations: A Cloud Scheduler trigger is ENFORCED, not just displayed: "Add trigger" creates a Cloud Scheduler job whose httpTarget names this job's own Admin API v2 :run endpoint, and when that scheduler job fires (on its cron schedule, or via "Run now") the appliance's httpTarget delivery really calls jobs.run — a new execution starts, exactly like a real OIDC-authenticated Cloud Scheduler → Cloud Run Jobs binding.
Vyomi has no Eventarc backend, so event-based triggers (Pub/Sub, Storage, Audit Log events) are not modelled — only the Cloud Scheduler binding shown here.

gcp.run.workerpools.crud.title: Worker pools (create, list, delete)
limitations: Worker pool instance splits across revisions are not modelled; a worker pool always runs its current template.

gcp.run.domainmappings.crud.title: Domain mappings (map a custom domain to a service, DNS records)
limitations: Vyomi does not provision a real TLS certificate or serve traffic on the mapped domain; the DNS records it returns are illustrative.
